notes: digestVectors: body is the task-start attestation body (v1, 13 keys). expected.ok = digest and the exact preimage bytes (UTF8 domain albera.task-start-attestation.v1, 0x00, canonical map as in action-digest.mjs); otherwise expected.code (malformed | ttl) and field.
The C# twin is TaskStartAttestation.cs (digest vectors and verifyVectors). It reproduces every expected value here in the dotnet contract test.

verifyVectors: the public half of an EPHEMERAL ECDSA P-256 test key (publicKeySpki, base64 DER; the private key was discarded after signing, nothing secret is in this file) and signed envelopes made with it. For each case, verifyTaskStartAttestation(signed, { clock: now, verify: the pinned key under keyId, expected }) must give result: ok, or the code and field of the refusal. The signature is ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 over the canonical bytes, IEEE P1363 (64 bytes), unpadded base64url. Both the Node and C# implementations must reproduce every result.

A statement with network "present" / "unknown" or checkpointType "standard" verifies here (ok): whether it is ENOUGH is the Authority's rule (network none AND checkpointType production), not the verifier's.

The last three cases pin domain separation: a genuine network attestation (10-key body, network domain) is malformed here, and a task-start body signed or digested under the network domain does not verify.
